The matrix \(A\) has 3 horizontal lines (rows) and 4 vertical lines (columns).
The order of a matrix is written as (number of rows) \(\times\) (number of columns).
Hence the order of \(A\) is \(3 \times 4\).

The number of elements in a matrix equals (number of rows) \(\times\) (number of columns).
Here \(A\) has order \(3 \times 4\), so the number of elements \(= 3 \times 4 = 12\).

In \(a_{ij}\), \(i\) is the row number and \(j\) is the column number.
\(a_{13}\) = row 1, column 3 \(= 19\).
\(a_{21}\) = row 2, column 1 \(= 35\).
\(a_{33}\) = row 3, column 3 \(= -5\).
\(a_{24}\) = row 2, column 4 \(= 12\).
\(a_{23}\) = row 2, column 3 \(= \frac{5}{2}\).

A matrix of order \(m \times n\) has \(mn\) elements, so the possible orders correspond to the ordered factor pairs of the number of elements.
24 elements: the ordered factorisations of 24 are \(1 \times 24,\ 2 \times 12,\ 3 \times 8,\ 4 \times 6,\ 6 \times 4,\ 8 \times 3,\ 12 \times 2,\ 24 \times 1\), giving 8 possible orders.
13 elements: 13 is prime, so the only ordered factor pairs are \(1 \times 13\) and \(13 \times 1\), giving 2 possible orders.

The possible orders \(m \times n\) correspond to the ordered factor pairs of the number of elements.
18 elements: \(1 \times 18,\ 2 \times 9,\ 3 \times 6,\ 6 \times 3,\ 9 \times 2,\ 18 \times 1\), giving 6 possible orders.
5 elements: 5 is prime, so \(1 \times 5\) and \(5 \times 1\), giving 2 possible orders.

Here \(a_{ij} = \frac{1}{2}\lvert -3i + j \rvert\) with \(i \in \{1,2,3\}\) and \(j \in \{1,2,3,4\}\).
Row 1 \((i=1)\): \(\frac{1}{2}\lvert -2 \rvert = 1,\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert -1 \rvert = \frac{1}{2},\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert 0 \rvert = 0,\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert 1 \rvert = \frac{1}{2}\).
Row 2 \((i=2)\): \(\frac{1}{2}\lvert -5 \rvert = \frac{5}{2},\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert -4 \rvert = 2,\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert -3 \rvert = \frac{3}{2},\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert -2 \rvert = 1\).
Row 3 \((i=3)\): \(\frac{1}{2}\lvert -8 \rvert = 4,\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert -7 \rvert = \frac{7}{2},\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert -6 \rvert = 3,\ \frac{1}{2}\lvert -5 \rvert = \frac{5}{2}\).
Hence \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{5}{2} & 2 & \frac{3}{2} & 1 \\ 4 & \frac{7}{2} & 3 & \frac{5}{2} \end{bmatrix}\).

Two matrices are equal when their corresponding elements are equal.
Comparing \(\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ x & 5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} y & z \\ 1 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\): from the top row \(y = 4\) and \(z = 3\); from the bottom row \(x = 1\).
Hence \(x = 1,\ y = 4,\ z = 3\).

Equate corresponding elements of \(\begin{bmatrix} x+y & 2 \\ 5+z & xy \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 2 \\ 5 & 8 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(5 + z = 5 \Rightarrow z = 0\).
\(x + y = 6\) and \(xy = 8\).
So \(x\) and \(y\) are roots of \(t^{2} - 6t + 8 = 0\), i.e. \((t-2)(t-4) = 0\), giving \(t = 2\) or \(t = 4\).
Hence \(x = 2,\ y = 4,\ z = 0\) or \(x = 4,\ y = 2,\ z = 0\).

Equate corresponding elements of \(\begin{bmatrix} x+y+z \\ x+z \\ y+z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ 5 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(x+y+z = 9\) ... (1)
\(x+z = 5\) ... (2)
\(y+z = 7\) ... (3)
Subtracting (2) from (1): \(y = 9 - 5 = 4\).
From (3): \(z = 7 - y = 7 - 4 = 3\).
From (2): \(x = 5 - z = 5 - 3 = 2\).
Hence \(x = 2,\ y = 4,\ z = 3\).

Equate corresponding elements of \(\begin{bmatrix} a-b & 2a+c \\ 2a-b & 3c+d \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 13 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(a - b = -1\) ... (1)
\(2a + c = 5\) ... (2)
\(2a - b = 0\) ... (3)
\(3c + d = 13\) ... (4)
Subtracting (1) from (3): \((2a - b) - (a - b) = 0 - (-1)\), so \(a = 1\).
From (1): \(b = a + 1 = 2\).
From (2): \(c = 5 - 2a = 3\).
From (4): \(d = 13 - 3c = 13 - 9 = 4\).
Hence \(a = 1,\ b = 2,\ c = 3,\ d = 4\).

Add corresponding elements:
\(A + B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2+1 & 4+3 \\ 3+(-2) & 2+5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 7 \\ 1 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\).

Subtract corresponding elements:
\(A - B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2-1 & 4-3 \\ 3-(-2) & 2-5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 5 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\).

First scale \(A\) by 3: \(3A = 3\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 12 \\ 9 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(3A - C = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 12 \\ 9 & 6 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6-(-2) & 12-5 \\ 9-3 & 6-4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 8 & 7 \\ 6 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\).

Add corresponding elements:
\(\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ -b & a \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ b & a \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} a+a & b+b \\ -b+b & a+a \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2a & 2b \\ 0 & 2a \end{bmatrix}\).

Add corresponding elements and use the identities \((p+q)^{2} = p^{2}+2pq+q^{2}\) and \((p-q)^{2} = p^{2}-2pq+q^{2}\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} a^{2}+b^{2} & b^{2}+c^{2} \\ a^{2}+c^{2} & a^{2}+b^{2} \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2ab & 2bc \\ -2ac & -2ab \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} a^{2}+b^{2}+2ab & b^{2}+c^{2}+2bc \\ a^{2}+c^{2}-2ac & a^{2}+b^{2}-2ab \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence the sum is \(\begin{bmatrix} (a+b)^{2} & (b+c)^{2} \\ (a-c)^{2} & (a-b)^{2} \end{bmatrix}\).

Add corresponding elements:
\(\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 4 & -6 \\ 8 & 5 & 16 \\ 2 & 8 & 5 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 12 & 7 & 6 \\ 8 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 11 & 11 & 0 \\ 16 & 5 & 21 \\ 5 & 10 & 9 \end{bmatrix}\).

Add corresponding elements and use \(\sin^{2} x + \cos^{2} x = 1\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} \cos^{2} x & \sin^{2} x \\ \sin^{2} x & \cos^{2} x \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} \sin^{2} x & \cos^{2} x \\ \cos^{2} x & \sin^{2} x \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos^{2}x+\sin^{2}x & \sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x \\ \sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x & \cos^{2}x+\sin^{2}x \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(A + B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 2 & 7 \\ 3 & -1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(B - C = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\).
Verification:
\(A + (B - C) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 9 & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((A + B) - C = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 2 & 7 \\ 3 & -1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 9 & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
Both sides are equal, so \(A + (B - C) = (A + B) - C\).

Multiplying \(A\) by 3 and \(B\) by 5 clears the denominators:
\(3A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 7 & 6 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(5B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 7 & 6 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(3A - 5B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 7 & 6 & 2 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 7 & 6 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\).

Multiply each matrix by its scalar.
\(\cos\theta \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & \sin\theta \\ -\sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos^{2}\theta & \sin\theta\cos\theta \\ -\sin\theta\cos\theta & \cos^{2}\theta \end{bmatrix}\).
\(\sin\theta \begin{bmatrix} \sin\theta & -\cos\theta \\ \cos\theta & \sin\theta \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \sin^{2}\theta & -\sin\theta\cos\theta \\ \sin\theta\cos\theta & \sin^{2}\theta \end{bmatrix}\).
Adding and using \(\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} \cos^{2}\theta+\sin^{2}\theta & \sin\theta\cos\theta-\sin\theta\cos\theta \\ -\sin\theta\cos\theta+\sin\theta\cos\theta & \cos^{2}\theta+\sin^{2}\theta \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).

Adding the two equations: \((X + Y) + (X - Y) = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), i.e. \(2X = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & 0 \\ 2 & 8 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(X = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\).
Subtracting the two equations: \((X + Y) - (X - Y) = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), i.e. \(2Y = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(Y = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).

Let \(P = 2X + 3Y = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(Q = 3X + 2Y = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
Compute \(3P - 2Q\) to eliminate \(X\): \((6X + 9Y) - (6X + 4Y) = 5Y\).
\(3P = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 9 \\ 12 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), \(2Q = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -4 \\ -2 & 10 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(5Y = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 13 \\ 14 & -10 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(Y = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{2}{5} & \frac{13}{5} \\ \frac{14}{5} & -2 \end{bmatrix}\).
Compute \(2P - 3Q\) to eliminate \(Y\): \((4X + 6Y) - (9X + 6Y) = -5X\).
\(2P = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ 8 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), \(3Q = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -6 \\ -3 & 15 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(-5X = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 12 \\ 11 & -15 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(X = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{2}{5} & -\frac{12}{5} \\ -\frac{11}{5} & 3 \end{bmatrix}\).

From \(2X + Y = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), we get \(2X = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} - Y = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -2 \\ -4 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence \(X = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ -2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(2\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & x \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} y & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 2x \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} y & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2+y & 6 \\ 1 & 2x+2 \end{bmatrix}\).
Equating with \(\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 1 & 8 \end{bmatrix}\): \(2 + y = 5 \Rightarrow y = 3\) and \(2x + 2 = 8 \Rightarrow x = 3\).
Hence \(x = 3,\ y = 3\).

\(2\begin{bmatrix} x & z \\ y & t \end{bmatrix} + 3\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2x+3 & 2z-3 \\ 2y & 2t+6 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(3\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 4 & 6 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 15 \\ 12 & 18 \end{bmatrix}\).
Equating corresponding elements:
\(2x + 3 = 9 \Rightarrow x = 3\).
\(2z - 3 = 15 \Rightarrow z = 9\).
\(2y = 12 \Rightarrow y = 6\).
\(2t + 6 = 18 \Rightarrow t = 6\).
Hence \(x = 3,\ y = 6,\ z = 9,\ t = 6\).

\(x\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + y\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2x - y \\ 3x + y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
So \(2x - y = 10\) and \(3x + y = 5\).
Adding the two equations: \(5x = 15 \Rightarrow x = 3\).
Then \(y = 2x - 10 = 6 - 10 = -4\).
Hence \(x = 3,\ y = -4\).

\(3\begin{bmatrix} x & y \\ z & w \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3x & 3y \\ 3z & 3w \end{bmatrix}\), and the right side is \(\begin{bmatrix} x & 6 \\ -1 & 2w \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 4 & x+y \\ z+w & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} x+4 & x+y+6 \\ z+w-1 & 2w+3 \end{bmatrix}\).
Equating corresponding elements:
\(3x = x + 4 \Rightarrow x = 2\).
\(3w = 2w + 3 \Rightarrow w = 3\).
\(3y = x + y + 6 \Rightarrow 2y = 2 + 6 = 8 \Rightarrow y = 4\).
\(3z = z + w - 1 \Rightarrow 2z = 3 - 1 = 2 \Rightarrow z = 1\).
Hence \(x = 2,\ y = 4,\ z = 1,\ w = 3\).
